title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - Manufacturing
description: Curated OT/ICS cybersecurity advisories, incidents and threat intelligence from primary sources. Editorial summaries by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

_otthreatfeed.usage: Free to reuse with attribution. Credit 'Mike Holcomb & UtilSec' and link back to otthreatfeed.com and to each item's linked primary source. Summaries are editorial paraphrase - verify against the primary source before acting.

items.title: PHP2Shell is now in KEV and under attack on exposed Palo Alto firewall management, and Siemens, Schneider Electric and ABB list affected OT products
items.content_text: CISA added both PHP2Shell flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 26 October with a federal deadline of 29 October. They allow unauthenticated remote code execution on servers running PHP and carry CVSS v4.0 9.2 (PHP Group); PHP fixed them on 21 October in 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. Researchers at Perplexity (Adel Karimi), with Expel’s Marcus Hutchins concurring, confirmed working remote code execution against a honeypot over 24–25 October; Sophos and Unit 42 withdrew earlier reports of successful exploitation, no victim organisation has been named, and CISA did not describe the activity. Palo Alto Networks’ advisory, updated 27–28 October, reports active exploitation targeting PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet. The web UI and XML API on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and Panorama are affected and GlobalProtect is not; Palo Alto raised the issue to Critical on 27 October, and its score falls to 5.2 when management access is limited to a jump host. Hotfixes such as 12.2.4-h1, 11.1.16-h4 and 10.2.18-h13 are out, a few more are due 29–30 October, and they also cover the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497, in KEV since 27 October.

items.title: Microsoft ties the ConnectWise Cloud Backup compromise to China-aligned Storm-0940 and lists manufacturing, automotive, chemicals and semiconductors among its targets
items.content_text: Microsoft said on 21 October that it assesses Storm-0940, which it calls a China-state aligned actor active since 2021, was responsible for the recently disclosed ConnectWise supply-chain compromise. The attackers controlled the identities of several ConnectWise cloud applications tied to Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) and used them to sign in to customers’ Microsoft 365 tenants as the application, so MFA did not apply; a separate password spray on 10–14 October did not succeed. Microsoft says attempts reached more than 2,250 tenants, that most of the targeting failed, and that in several cases privileged access followed in under three hours. It says the actor used ARTEX, an open-source penetration-testing framework that can drive any AI model, and lists aerospace and defense, automotive, chemicals, energy, manufacturing and semiconductors among targeted sectors. ConnectWise, which first detected the activity on 14 October, suspended Cloud Backup and shut down SaaS Security and Cloud Management; its chief executive said on 22 October that services are being restored in controlled phases, and the company says it has no evidence that partner backup data was compromised. Huntress reported unauthorized sign-ins at 162 tenants it monitors. No manufacturing victim or OT impact has been named. Manufacturers whose MSP manages Microsoft 365 through these services should check their tenants (editorial assessment).

items.title: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed credential theft against FortiGate gateways is still running, with targets in all 16 critical-infrastructure sectors
items.content_text: The FBI and US Secret Service warned on 6 October, in joint advisory JCSA-20261006-01, that the FortiBleed campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPNs remains an active threat. There is no CVE: the agencies describe abuse of reused or leaked credentials and legacy SHA-256 password storage, and researchers describe password spraying and stuffing, offline cracking of extracted hashes and a sniffer that captures authentication traffic. Attackers have added admin accounts and deleted or reset legitimate ones, locking owners out. The agencies say targets span all 16 US critical-infrastructure sectors, critical manufacturing among them, and the FBI ties the access to Payload ransomware; SOCRadar, which reports overlaps with INC and Lynx, says it has confirmed at least 12 ransomware deployments from this access and counted 86,644 working device credentials across 194 countries as of 19 June. No OT system compromise has been described. FortiGate often sits at the IT/OT boundary in plants, so a stolen admin login there is a path toward production networks (editorial assessment).

items.title: ESET documents the first destructive attack by a Belarus-aligned group in Europe, against a Ukrainian manufacturer, and a Sandworm wiper attack built on another group’s access
items.content_text: ESET’s APT Activity Report for April to September 2026, published 28 October, says the Belarus-aligned group FrostyNeighbor attacked a Ukrainian manufacturing company that plays an important role in the country’s transportation sector. ESET calls it the first destructive cyberattack by a Belarus-aligned actor that it has documented in the European theatre, and a notable escalation, because destructive operations in Ukraine had until now been tied to Russia-aligned groups. The report gives no date, malware or account of the effect on production or control systems, and it does not name the company.

items.title: Symantec: Russia’s APT28 spent at least two months inside a NATO naval shipbuilder’s network and also hit a military aircraft-engine maker
items.content_text: Symantec reported on 20 October that Swallowtail, which it equates with APT28 (Fancy Bear, Forest Blizzard; the US government considers it a GRU unit), broke into a naval shipbuilder and a manufacturer of military aircraft engines, as well as a law-enforcement agency, in two unnamed NATO member states. At the shipbuilder, a macro-laden Word attachment opened on 24 July dropped the Hookedge backdoor; within days the operators set up a persistent SSH tunnel, ran a PowerShell script to capture NTLM credentials and mapped internal DNS and privileges, and on 31 July deployed a previously undocumented loader whose payload was not recovered. The launcher was last seen on 24 September. Symantec reports IT-network reconnaissance and credential capture only: no OT, ICS or production impact and no confirmed data theft, and it names no victim. It has published indicators, which defence and aerospace suppliers should check against their own networks (editorial assessment).

items.title: Attackers took over refrigeration controllers in about 700 French supermarkets; plants run similar web-managed controllers
items.content_text: Over the nights of 11–13 October, attackers remotely changed settings on web-managed refrigeration controllers in French supermarkets, stretching defrost cycles so that some cabinets reached about 50°C, spoiling stock and, according to the Paris prosecutor, starting fires at some stores. Finance Minister Roland Lescure put the toll at about 700 stores on 13 October, across Carrefour, Coopérative U, E.Leclerc, Intermarché/Netto and Monoprix. CERT-FR’s alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 named Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers on 12 October, added Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb on 13 October, and on 16 October said attack campaigns are probably still ongoing; the alert was still at that version on 28 October, and no new attack nights have been reported after 13 October. Danfoss says most affected units are end-of-life or on outdated firmware, and Copeland points to a discontinued, end-of-life generation. No group has claimed it, no ransom was demanded and the entry route is not established. On 22 October Forescout counted 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration-management service observations on 6,017 IP addresses in 99 countries, found about 80% of observed Danfoss AK-SM 800A StoreView services on firmware older than 4.3.1, and named food processing among the sectors at risk. This is a food-retail incident, not a manufacturing one; we carry it because plants run cold rooms, chillers and building systems from similar web-managed controllers, and any that are reachable from the internet face the same risk (editorial assessment).

items.title: US, UK and German agencies warn that SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024, getting in through stolen credentials and old edge-device flaws
items.content_text: CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service, with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, issued advisory AA26-293A on 20 October about SafePay, a closed ransomware group with no affiliates. The agencies count at least 600 victim organizations across multiple critical-infrastructure sectors in the Americas, Europe and Australia since August 2024. SafePay gets in with exposed or brute-forced credentials, phished accounts and VPN logins, often from Mullvad addresses, and by exploiting older edge-device flaws, including CVE-2020-3259 and CVE-2023-20269. Once inside it uses WinRM, PsExec and RDP, takes data with tools such as RClone and WinSCP, deletes shadow copies and resets NAS devices that hold backups, then encrypts and threatens to leak. As reported, the advisory names no sectors or victims. We carry it because manufacturing was again the sector most often posted on ransomware leak sites in the third quarter, by NordLayer’s count, and SafePay’s entry points are the VPNs and remote-access gear that front many plants (editorial assessment).

items.title: SOCRadar finds ransomware affiliates running intrusions through an AI-agent framework, with industrial and manufacturing firms the largest group among 62 targets
items.content_text: SOCRadar’s threat researchers reported on 20 October, and updated on 23 October, what they found on an exposed server holding a Russian-speaking operator’s logs: intrusions carried out for affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups through “Phantom”, an AI kill-chain framework that planned each stage, wrote commands and sorted stolen data, with the operator approving every step. SOCRadar identified 62 named target organisations, 36 of them in the US; industrial and manufacturing organisations were the largest group, at about 16%, and four victims were later posted on leak sites. According to the operator’s own records, which SOCRadar could not verify, initial access came through three flaws that are all in CISA’s KEV catalog: FortiClient EMS CVE-2026-35616, SimpleHelp CVE-2024-57727 and cPanel/WHM CVE-2026-41940. SOCRadar sees a shared operating environment between the two groups but has low confidence in any formal alliance. No OT or ICS impact is described. The same internet-facing management and remote-support tools are common at plants (editorial assessment).

items.title: In lab tests, an AI model found and moved a robotic arm within minutes, and an AI coding agent rebuilt a published controller exploit for about $6
items.content_text: Booz Allen’s 8 October report describes frontier AI models tested in its isolated, multi-vendor OT lab, which is modelled on a manufacturing facility. Across eight scenarios the models met every test objective; in one they went from a perimeter compromise to actions inside the industrial control network in just over 16 minutes, with a human approving every exploit and any action with a physical effect. One model identified a robotic arm, mapped its protection zones and motion limits and moved it within minutes; in another test the models found live, pre-authenticated connections to 14 OT devices. Some controls held: a controller rejected a stop command and a motor in local-control mode refused remote starts. A Booz Allen researcher told Dark Reading that removing the approval step would roughly halve the time, and Industrial Cyber reports that the company calls the findings preliminary. Separately, Claroty’s Team82 reported on 13 October that an AI coding agent, redirected by a researcher and connected to the Ghidra reverse-engineering tool, reproduced three previously disclosed Danfoss AK-SM 800A flaws and chained them to root on a lab device in about 28 minutes for roughly $6 of usage, working from publicly downloadable firmware. Team82 stresses this was not autonomous discovery and does not link the flaws to the French supermarket attacks. Both are lab results, not real-world attacks.

items.title: Nozomi’s summer telemetry puts manufacturing first for OT/IoT alerts per organization, with credential techniques about a third of detections
items.content_text: Nozomi Networks Labs’ review of June–August 2026 customer telemetry, published 12 October, ranks manufacturing first for alerts per organization, ahead of transportation and of energy, utilities and waste, which moved up to third. Credential-related techniques made up roughly a third of detections. Among alerts Nozomi attributed to named actors, Scattered Spider accounted for close to half, and Russia-linked or Russian-speaking actors together for more than a third. Siemens PLCs and Rockwell products were among the vulnerable products detected most often, and Nozomi says 58% of 2026 vulnerabilities rate High or Critical, against 48% in 2025. Alerts per organization measures what sensors flag in customer networks, not confirmed intrusions.

items.title: Kaspersky shows how Bluetooth barcode-scanner base stations can type commands into warehouse PCs; Honeywell has fixed its flaw
items.content_text: Kaspersky published a warehouse security audit on 20 October showing that Bluetooth base stations for handheld barcode scanners can be used to run commands on the PC they are plugged into. The Honeywell flaw behind it, CVE-2026-4272, is missing authentication in handheld-scanner base stations: an attacker within Bluetooth range can execute commands on the connected host without logging in. Honeywell rates it CVSS v3.1 8.1 and has released fixed base-station firmware (C1 Base GK000432BAA, D1 Base HE000085BAA and A1/B1 Base BK000763BAA_BK000765BAA_CU000101BAA). The CVE was published in April, it is not in KEV, and no exploitation is known. Kaspersky says the same weakness appears with other vendors, citing a Zebra ZQ630 printer that accepted app uploads over Bluetooth (no CVE). The foothold is a trusted warehouse PC rather than a controller, but shipping, receiving and line-side PCs often share networks with production systems (editorial assessment).

items.title: NordLayer counts 2,894 ransomware attacks in the third quarter, and manufacturing is again the most-targeted sector with 347
items.content_text: NordLayer’s ransomware statistics for July to September 2026, compiled from leak-site postings and updated in October, count 2,894 attacks, almost 50% more than a year earlier. The Gentlemen (383) and Qilin (363) led, followed by INC Ransom (110) and Krybit (95, a figure NordLayer says may be inflated). Manufacturing remained the most-targeted sector with 347 attacks, roughly 18–19% of the total, ahead of IT with 210. NordLayer’s own figures for manufacturing’s change from the previous quarter do not reconcile, so we leave that trend out. These are attacks claimed on leak sites, not confirmed production outages.

items.title: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain gave attackers root on fully patched VPNs, and one link is still unpatched
items.content_text: Ivanti disclosed on 13 October that a chain of three flaws was used against a limited number of Connect Secure customers to run commands as root on fully patched appliances. Two of the flaws are fixed under one CVE, CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS v3.1 8.6), which CISA added to KEV the same day with a 16 October deadline; the third, a privilege escalation, has no CVE and no patch yet. Volexity found the chain while handling a customer incident and tracks the attacker as UTA0576, a new cluster; exploitation dates to at least early October (1–3 October). The intruders stole domain credentials, searched Active Directory for LAPS passwords and BitLocker keys, sprayed passwords and wiped logs, leaving no web shell. CISA and Volexity warn that Ivanti’s Integrity Checker may miss the compromise. Volexity said on 13 October that the third flaw would be patched “in the coming weeks”; no Ivanti fix for it had been found as of 28 October. No manufacturer has been named, but Connect Secure often carries engineer and integrator remote access into plant networks (editorial assessment).

items.title: SD-WAN controllers are under attack: Arista’s VeloCloud Orchestrator joins Cisco SD-WAN Manager in KEV, alongside an exploited FortiMail flaw
items.content_text: Arista disclosed on 22 October, in Security Advisory 0199, that CVE-2026-114625, an SQL injection in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator, lets any authenticated user gain operator privileges. Arista rates it CVSS v3.1 9.9 (v4.0 9.4) and fixes it in 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; its hosted orchestrators are already patched. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 23 October with a 26 October deadline, which has passed. Cisco disclosed on 30 September that CVE-2026-76504 in Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, an improper handling of URI encoding, lets an unauthenticated remote attacker bypass an authentication rule on an API endpoint and gain administrator-level access. Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in September, scores the flaw CVSS 9.8, lists no workarounds and fixes it in 20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 and 26.2.1; releases older than 20.9 must migrate. It revised the advisory on 2 October, and CISA added the flaw to KEV on 30 September with a 3 October deadline. BleepingComputer counts it as the fifth exploited SD-WAN zero-day of 2026. Separately, Fortinet’s FG-IR-26-175 (1 October) covers CVE-2026-104286 in FortiMail, a path traversal that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests (CVSS 9.8). Fortinet says it has been reported as exploited in the wild, and CISA listed it in KEV the same day with a 4 October deadline. Fortinet’s 5 October update lists fixed releases 7.4.9, 7.6.7 and 8.0.2, with 7.2 users told to move to 7.4 or later. None of the vendors names an actor or victims. For multi-site manufacturers, an SD-WAN orchestrator or manager configures the links between plants, warehouses and head office, so admin access there reaches every site at once (editorial assessment).

items.title: Citrix patches a fourth critical NetScaler flaw, CVE-2026-107406, while the campaign behind three exploited zero-days continues
items.content_text: Citrix published bulletin CTX697191 on 8 October for CVE-2026-107406 (CVSS v4.0 9.5), a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway set up as a SAML service provider or identity provider that Citrix says may lead to code execution or denial of service. It is not reported exploited and is not in KEV as of CISA’s 27 October catalog, but the builds that fixed the September zero-days (14.1-73.37 to 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.23 to 13.1-64.28) stay vulnerable when used as a SAML identity provider, so those appliances need another upgrade. The campaign itself runs on the three earlier flaws: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 (KEV 27 September) and CVE-2026-88779 (KEV 4 October), which Citrix and watchTowr describe as a denial-of-service bug; CISA says attackers use it to force reboots so that code planted through CVE-2026-88771 runs. Mandiant counts dozens of victim organizations and describes suspected state-nexus actors without naming a group; Arctic Wolf counts at least 78 targeted organizations, and Shadowserver sees more than 20,000 exposed instances. No manufacturer has been named. NetScaler Gateway commonly fronts contractor and remote-engineer access into plant DMZs (editorial assessment).

items.title: Siemens: critical web-server flaws in S7-1500 and ET 200SP CPUs have no fix yet, alongside TM MFP and Industrial Edge advisories
items.content_text: Siemens’ 13 October release (17 advisories by SecurityWeek’s count) includes SSA-591731: eight web-server flaws, CVE-2026-63350 to CVE-2026-63357, across all versions of S7-1500, ET 200SP, ET 200pro and Drive Controller CPUs, rated CVSS v3.1 9.6 (v4.0 9.4). An attacker could run code in an authorized user’s browser and carry out PLC operations with that user’s rights; there is no fix yet, only mitigations. SSA-784472 lists 377 CVEs, the highest rated CVSS v3.1 10.0, in the optional GNU/Linux subsystem of the S7-1500 TM MFP technology module, also without a fix. SSA-832641 covers authenticated path traversal in Industrial Edge devices (CVE-2026-44415, CVSS v3.1 9.1) that can expose or delete data; fixes are out for Industrial Edge devices, IoT2050 and several SIMATIC IPCs, but not yet for SCALANCE LPE9413/9433 or the affected HMI panels. None of these Siemens flaws is reported exploited or listed in KEV (the exploited Software Center flaw in the top story is separate). CISA republished the October advisories on 22 October as ICSA-26-295-02 to -18, and its versions still show no fix for the S7 PLC web server, the GNU/Linux subsystems of the S7-1500 TM MFP and CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP, or WinCC V7.5 (CVE-2026-59241, CVSS v3.1 8.8; WinCC V8.0 Update 11 and V8.1 Update 7 are fixed). The S7-1500 is one of the most widely used PLC families on production lines, so its web server is the item to check first (editorial assessment).

items.title: Attackers are abusing a Siemens Software Center flaw in ClickFix malware campaigns, and CISA has added it to KEV with a 3 November deadline
items.content_text: Siemens confirmed on 19 October that CVE-2026-110936, a DLL search-path flaw in Siemens Software Center, its tool for downloading, installing and activating purchased software, is being exploited in what it calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign. Attackers ship a genuine, validly signed copy of the program with their own DLLs in an installer; when a user is talked into running it, the program loads the attackers’ code, even on PCs that never had Software Center. Siemens says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached, and it names no malware family; its advisory was still at V1.2 of 19 October on 28 October. The flaw is rated CVSS v3.1 6.7 (v4.0 8.4); V4.0.9.8 fixes it, and existing installs update on next start. CISA added it to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November deadline and republished the advisory on 22 October, listing critical manufacturing among affected sectors. No targets are named, but a trusted Siemens signature makes such a lure more convincing to plant engineers (editorial assessment).

items.title: BeyondTrust Remote Support and a FortiOS flaw join KEV, and Unit 42 says Qilin and INC use a GlobalProtect bug to get VPN sessions past MFA
items.content_text: CISA added BeyondTrust Remote Support CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS v4.0 9.3) to KEV on 16 October with a 19 October deadline. Google’s Threat Intelligence Group says the suspected PRC-nexus actor ARMORY CASTLE (formerly UNC5221) exploited it as a zero-day from late August to gain root, harvest credentials and delete logs; BeyondTrust shipped patch BT26-05-RS on 8 October, and self-hosted appliances without auto-update must be patched by hand. The same day CISA listed Fortinet CVE-2025-61624, an authenticated FortiOS CLI path traversal that Fortinet rates Medium and fixed in April. Unit 42 reported on 14 October that attackers who broke into a telecom managed-service provider through FortiManager (CVE-2024-47575) used it to gain root on managed FortiGates; configuration and credential material for more than 500 FortiGates was exposed, though Unit 42 does not confirm intrusion into those customer networks and names no state. The CVE record lists Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 units running FortiOS as affected. On 19–20 October Unit 42 reported that Qilin and INC ransomware exploit GlobalProtect CVE-2026-0257, patched in May, to open VPN sessions past MFA and then move to vCenter, ESXi and Veeam, with manufacturing among targeted sectors. PAN-OS CVE-2026-0322 has been in KEV since 14 October, and exposed PAN-OS management interfaces are now also under attack through PHP2Shell (see the top story). Some feeds claim SonicWall SMA1000’s CVE-2026-102255 is now exploited, but that is unconfirmed and the flaw is not in KEV. OEMs, MSPs and integrators often reach plant networks through tools like these (editorial assessment).

items.title: Mitsubishi Electric fixes an authentication bypass in ICONICS GENESIS SCADA software, but MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will get no fix
items.content_text: Mitsubishi Electric’s advisory 2026-006, published 15 October, covers flaws across the ICONICS GENESIS64 and GENESIS SCADA and HMI suite. CVE-2026-16436 (CVSS v4.0 9.2) is an authentication bypass: a shared, fixed challenge-response can unlock any user account, although a remote attacker must first obtain that response. CVE-2026-16438 (v4.0 9.4) concerns default DCOM permissions granted to the administrator account, CVE-2026-16437 (v4.0 7.1) lets an administrator read or write the challenge-response file, and the older libwebp flaw CVE-2023-4863 (v4.0 9.3) affects ICONICS Suite 10.97 to 10.97.2 if a local administrator imports a crafted file. Affected are GENESIS 11.03 and earlier; GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and IoTWorX 10.97.3 and earlier; and all versions of MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz. Fixes are ICONICS Suite and IoTWorX 10.98, GENESIS 11.04 and, for libwebp, ICONICS Suite 10.97.3; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz will not be fixed. CISA republished the advisory on 27 October as ICSA-26-300-02, listing CVSS v3.1 scores of 9.1 for CVE-2026-16438, 8.1 for CVE-2026-16436, 6.4 for CVE-2026-16437 and 8.2 for CVE-2023-4863. No exploitation is reported. GENESIS64 and Hyper Historian commonly run plant HMIs and historians (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA: a WAGO controller flaw lets a low-privileged user run commands as root, a Moxa edge gateway has a hard-coded key, and PCAN drivers can crash Windows
items.content_text: CISA’s 20 October batch republished WAGO’s CERT@VDE advisory VDE-2026-096 as ICSA-26-293-02. On CC100, PFC100 G2, PFC200 G2, TP600, Edge Controller and WP400 devices below firmware 4.10.0 (FW32), CVE-2026-80466 (CVSS v3.1 8.8) lets a low-privileged remote user inject operating-system commands through the routing settings of the web-based management, which a root helper script then runs; CVE-2026-88850 (v3.1 8.1) lets low-privileged users change root-owned PROFIBUS parameters. The fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32), the release that also fixes the CODESYS issues WAGO disclosed on 1 October. ICSA-26-293-03 covers the Moxa AIG-302 edge gateway with ThingsPro Edge 1.4.0 and earlier: CVE-2026-109813 is a hard-coded cryptographic key (v3.1 8.1, v4.0 8.6) and CVE-2026-109812 a missing-authorization flaw (v3.1 6.8, v4.0 6.9), both fixed in 1.4.1. ICSA-26-293-01 covers six local flaws in HMS Networks’ PEAK-System PCAN CAN-interface drivers for Windows (5.1.2 and earlier) that can crash the kernel, the highest CVE-2026-103672 at v3.1 7.1; CISA says they are not remotely exploitable, and 5.1.4 fixes them. CISA lists critical manufacturing among affected sectors for all three, and none is reported exploited.

items.title: Rockwell fixes an ArmorBlock I/O flaw that lets anyone reset its web password; Schneider and ABB flag HMI and account-takeover bugs
items.content_text: Rockwell’s only new October advisory, SD1801, covers 1732E ArmorBlock I/O modules on firmware 3.012 and earlier. CVE-2026-12655 (CVSS v3.1 9.1, v4.0 8.8) is a capture-replay authentication bypass that lets an unauthenticated attacker change the web-server password and take over the module’s admin account; CVE-2026-12656 (CVSS v3.1 7.5) is a network-storm denial of service that needs a power cycle to clear. Rockwell found both internally, fixes them in firmware 3.013 and lists no workaround. Schneider Electric’s SEVD-2026-286-01 (13 October) says an unmaintained third-party component in Pro-face STW6000 and Harmony STW6 HMIs (all versions; CVE-2026-96434, CVSS v3.1 8.8) could let an attacker take control of the panel if a user visits a malicious web page. SecurityWeek’s 14 October roundup adds that ABB’s dynovaPRO advisory covers the Keycloak password-reset bypass CVE-2026-18963 (CVSS 9.1, first published in August); ABB knows of no exploitation, but its logs show 26 password-change events across nine customers that may be testing. ArmorBlock modules sit on machines on the plant floor, so admin takeover lets an attacker change I/O configuration inside the cell (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA: Red Lion N-Tron 700 switches keep factory admin logins active and accept unauthenticated SNMP changes; the fix is firmware 3.11.1
items.content_text: CISA’s ICSA-26-281-01 (8 October; Update A on 15 October revised the CVSS v4.0 scores) covers seven flaws in Red Lion (HMS Networks) N-Tron 700 Series industrial Ethernet switches, reported by Idaho National Laboratory. The factory default admin credentials stay active after other administrators are configured; SNMP can change configuration, accounts and firmware without authentication and can trigger a TFTP export of plaintext credentials; firmware and bootloader updates are neither signed nor authenticated; and a URL can reboot the switch. The authentication bypass requires physical access. The highest CVSS v3.1 score is 8.3, with v4.0 scores up to 9.3 in the CVE records. Firmware 3.11.0 and earlier and bootloader 2.0.6.1 and earlier are affected, and the fix is firmware 3.11.1 or later. CISA lists critical manufacturing among the affected sectors and knows of no public exploitation. A compromised switch can expose or reroute traffic between controllers and HMIs (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA flags an Ignition privilege-escalation flaw, six bugs in the Eclipse Milo OPC UA library and end-of-life EasyIO controllers that will not be fixed
items.content_text: On 13 October CISA published ICSA-26-286-01 for Inductive Automation’s Ignition SCADA/HMI platform: CVE-2026-92817 (CVSS v3.1 8.8, v4.0 8.7) is an incorrect-authorization flaw that allows privilege escalation in versions 8.1.0–8.1.54 and 8.3.0–8.3.8, fixed in 8.1.55 and 8.3.9. On 15 October ICSA-26-288-01 covered six flaws in Eclipse Milo, the open-source Java OPC UA client and server library, the worst a missing-authorization bug at CVSS v3.1 8.2; version 1.1.5 fixes them and the 0.6.x line will not be fixed. Exposure depends on which OT products embed Milo, so expect follow-on vendor notices. On 6 October CISA republished Johnson Controls’ notice for EasyIO FG controller firmware: hard-coded credentials and improper privilege management (CVE-2026-27872 and CVE-2026-27873, CVSS 7.7 each), which CISA says are not remotely exploitable. The product is end-of-life with no fix, and the vendor recommends moving to EasyIO Neo R1. CISA lists critical manufacturing among the sectors for all three and knows of no public exploitation.

items.title: WAGO fixes a CVSS 9.8 BACnet flaw that lets an unauthenticated attacker overwrite files on its controllers, as CODESYS patches its runtime and gateway
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published WAGO advisory VDE-2025-102 on 1 October for CVE-2025-41753 (CVSS 9.8), a path traversal in the BACnet/IP stack: because BACnet File Object names are not properly validated, an unauthenticated remote attacker can read or overwrite arbitrary files on the device, which WAGO says may lead to full system compromise. Affected are the 750-811x, 750-821x, 751-9x01, 752-8303 and 762 series on wago_os_linux below 4.8.9; the fix is firmware 4.8.9 (FW30). The same day WAGO published VDE-2025-081 for CODESYS Control flaws in the same device families (CVE-2025-41738, CVSS 8.3, plus two lower-rated bugs) that can cause denial of service or run code when a user opens a malicious CODESYS project file; the fix is firmware 4.10.0 (FW32). On 30 September CODESYS itself disclosed CVE-2026-79625 (CVSS 8.1), a race condition that lets an authenticated user with monitoring access cause incorrect data processing, malfunction or denial of service in the Control runtime, and CVE-2026-76992 (CVSS 7.5), which can exhaust memory in a CODESYS client that connects to an attacker-controlled gateway. Both are fixed in 3.5.22.40, with Linux, ARM and other platform variants due in 4.23.0.0 in Q4 2026. No exploitation is reported for any of them. Because the CODESYS runtime is licensed to other controller makers, watch for their follow-on advisories (editorial note).

items.title: CISA: four flaws in the EPICS Base control-system toolkit include a CVSS 9.8 integer overflow that may allow remote code execution; 7.0.11 fixes them
items.content_text: CISA published ICSA-26-300-01 on 27 October for EPICS Base 7.0.10 and earlier, the open-source toolkit used to build control systems at particle accelerators and large research facilities. CVE-2026-114595, an integer overflow that could lead to remote code execution, is rated CVSS v3.1 9.8 (v4.0 9.3) by CISA; CVE-2026-114596 is rated 8.2, and two out-of-bounds reads, CVE-2026-114597 and CVE-2026-114598, are rated 7.5 each. Version 7.0.11 fixes all four, and CISA reports no known exploitation. CISA lists critical manufacturing as the affected sector. EPICS is rare on commercial production lines; it matters most to manufacturers that run research, test or pilot facilities built on it (editorial assessment).

items.title: EmbedThis fixes critical flaws in the GoAhead embedded web server that device makers build into their products; CVE IDs are not yet public
items.content_text: EmbedThis published security advisories for its GoAhead embedded web server on 12 October and fixed several Critical flaws in version 6.1.1: acceptance of revoked client certificates on the OpenSSL backend (rated 9.1 by EmbedThis), command injection through CGI on Windows and an authentication bypass for users with BF1-hashed passwords, plus a High-rated mTLS chain-depth bypass with LibreSSL. FoxIO published a write-up of the TLS issues on 26 October, with proof-of-concept code and a fingerprinting tool. CVE IDs have not been published yet, so CVE-based scanners will not flag affected devices. EmbedThis lists Siemens, Rockwell, HP, Canon and D-Link among GoAhead users, but no device maker has been shown to ship an affected build, and device fixes depend on each manufacturer. No exploitation is reported.

items.title: Moxa fixes a remote-access client that can be tricked into trusting a fake server, and leaves an end-of-life cellular gateway with static keys unfixed
items.content_text: Moxa published two advisories on 27 October. CVE-2026-111459 (Moxa CVSS v4.0 7.6) affects MRC Client 1.0.0 to 4.2.0, the OpenVPN-based client for Moxa Remote Connect: it accepts a server-supplied configuration without proper certificate validation, so an attacker in the network path could impersonate the server. Version 4.2.2, available through Moxa support, fixes it. The OnCell G3150A-LTE cellular gateway has static HTTPS and CA private keys in its firmware (CVE-2026-111460, 7.7) and a command injection in its SMS-based upgrade function (CVE-2026-111461, 7.5); the product is end-of-life and will not be fixed, so Moxa advises resetting the device to regenerate its keys and keeping SMS disabled. No exploitation is reported. Remote-access clients and cellular gateways like these are common ways for machine builders and integrators to reach equipment on the plant floor (editorial assessment).

items.title: ABB flags an AC500 V3 visualization denial-of-service, an Automation Builder project-file flaw and an unpatched Mint Workbench I bug
items.content_text: ABB published two notifications on 28 September, for its AC500 V3 PLCs and the Automation Builder engineering suite. In AC500 V3, invalid type usage in the visualization component could let an attacker cause a denial of service (3ADR011565). In Automation Builder, deserialization of untrusted data means a crafted project file or project archive could execute arbitrary code (3ADR011566). On 29 September ABB revised its Mint Workbench I advisory (first issued 17 September) for CVE-2026-19438 (CVSS v3.1 7.5, v4 8.2), a path traversal that lets a local attacker who already has file-write access read arbitrary system files; version 5876 and earlier are affected. There is no patch: the product reaches end of life at the end of 2026 (2027 in China), and ABB’s workarounds are to disable the MWI http service when it is not in use, restrict physical access and keep User Account Control on. No exploitation is reported. The Automation Builder flaw is the one to watch on engineering workstations, since project files routinely move between integrators, machine builders and plant staff.

items.title: Murrelektronik says remove its AAS edge client: a CVSS 9.8 missing-authentication flaw lets anyone rewrite device data, and no fix is coming
items.content_text: CERT@VDE published Murrelektronik advisory VDE-2026-108 on 6 October for CVE-2026-94293 (CVSS 9.8), missing authentication in every version of the aas-edge-client reference implementation. An unauthenticated attacker can read and modify the Asset Administration Shell submodel data held on the edge device, and because changes are stored locally and forwarded to the central AAS server, connected systems may receive manipulated device information. There is no fix: Murrelektronik says the software was a reference implementation built for a trade-fair demonstrator and is no longer maintained, has archived its repositories and made them private, and tells users to stop using it and remove existing deployments. The Asset Administration Shell is an Industry 4.0 digital-twin standard, so the practical risk is reference code that was copied into a pilot or production data pipeline (editorial assessment).

items.title: Siemens fixes a SAML replay flaw in the Mendix SAML module, and ABB fixes a local missing-authentication flaw in Edgenius
items.content_text: Siemens SSA-137528 (26 October) covers CVE-2026-89209 in the Mendix SAML module, which lets a captured assertion be replayed in identity-provider-initiated sign-ins; Siemens rates it CVSS v3.1 6.8 (v4.0 7.6) and fixes it in Mendix SAML 3.6.29 for Mendix 9 and 4.2.4 for Mendix 10 and 11, or users can disable IdP-initiated single sign-on. ABB’s advisory 7PAA026271 (22 October) covers CVE-2026-13599, missing authentication in the Edge AuthDB component of ABB Ability Edgenius 3.2.3.0 and earlier (CVSS v3.1 7.8); an attacker needs local Linux access to a node, functional safety is not affected, and 3.2.4.1 fixes it, with a Kubernetes network-policy workaround. Neither flaw is reported exploited. Mendix is used to build shop-floor apps, and Edgenius hosts industrial edge applications (editorial assessment).

items.title: CISA’s final CIRCIA incident-reporting rule has reached White House review; who it covers will not be known until it is published
items.content_text: The Office of Information and Regulatory Affairs logged CISA’s final rule under the Cyber Incident Reporting for Critical Infrastructure Act (RIN 1670-AA04) for review on 1 October. The law sets 72-hour reporting for covered cyber incidents and 24-hour reporting for ransom payments by covered entities in critical-infrastructure sectors, which include critical manufacturing, but those duties start only on dates the final rule sets, and the text, including which entities are covered, is not public. The statutory deadline passed in October 2025, and HIPAA Journal reports publication is expected before year-end. In a report released 28 September from a July roundtable, GAO found that industry participants flagged the forthcoming CIRCIA rule and the SEC’s disclosure requirement as problems, citing differing thresholds, timelines and definitions. OIRA review is procedural, and the text can still change.

items.title: CISA’s new four-year strategy names OT security and consequence-based prioritisation, with a review of its core services due to start within 60 days
items.content_text: CISA released “CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail” on 26 October. Under its Defend pillar the agency lists protecting operational technology, including modernising OT environments and improving asset visibility and anomaly detection, alongside supply-chain integrity. It says it will move away from all-hazards approaches toward risk-informed, consequence-based analysis, and it supports a national risk register. CISA will begin a review of its core services within 60 days, deliver an implementation plan with metrics within 180 days and report progress after a year. The strategy creates no new legal obligations, and analysts quoted by GovInfoSecurity questioned whether the agency can deliver it after losing about a third of its staff.
